synopsis: A sleet-grey commuter line climbs onto a stone viaduct above the clouds and runs the length of halls the size of mountain ranges.

shots.prompt:
HOOK. Open already mid-motion on one ordinary object passing the glass at arm's length, so close and so fast it is only a streak. A dull, grey, utterly routine commute. At 1.5 seconds a two-note chime cuts in and a calm neutral announcer says the destination line. Nobody reacts and nothing changes. The train immediately accelerates hard. By 6 seconds ONE thing far ahead is unmistakably wrong, and it is already growing.

A sleet-grey suburban line in failing afternoon light. An allotment fence whips past the glass close enough to blur, a football pitch and a supermarket car park stripping backward, bare trees and a chalk ridge standing behind. The announcer says exactly: "Next stop: Valhalla." The train slams into acceleration. By 6 seconds the line has begun to climb and the sleet has turned to dry snow going horizontal past the window.

HARD BREACH. In the first half second something enormous slams past the glass at arm's length and blacks the frame out for an instant. Coming out of that darkness the ordinary world is already gone and the line has physically committed to the destination with no way back. The shot ends with the destination's first true landmark resolving far ahead.

The carriage judders hard as a stone embankment wall slams past the glass and blacks the frame. The line is climbing steeply now. Farmhouse lights drop away below the level of the track, snow streaks horizontally past the window, and a bare white ridge far ahead keeps growing as the train runs out onto a viaduct with nothing beneath it but cloud.

ARRIVAL EDGE. Open on a violent change of light in the first half second: the exposure blows out white or crushes to black and recovers. Then the first landmark grows continuously across the whole shot until it no longer fits inside the window. Show how far down or how far up the place goes. The scale must be frightening.

A violent jolt and the train breaks up through the cloud floor into blinding low sunlight. Above the deck the air is thin and the light is hard and raking. A dark shape on the snow plain resolves into a hall the size of a mountain range, its roof shingled in overlapping golden shields, growing until it no longer fits inside the window.

FLYTHROUGH. Open with that landmark's mass already passing the window at close range, filling the glass and strobing the interior. Maximum parallax: foreground elements cross the frame in a fraction of a second while the true size of the place is revealed by what lies beyond them. Something larger still is already visible ahead.

The carriage judders and the hall wall arrives at arm's length. Barn-door-sized hammered gold shields cross the glass one after another, firelight flashing between them across endless tables inside and strobing the carriage. Ravens cross close and fast. The sky above has gone deep bruise-dark and all the light in the frame is firelight. Beyond the receding wall three more halls stand out on the plain.

DEEPEST SCALE. Open with a hard impact against the glass in the first half second - heat, pressure, spray or a shockwave that jolts the camera and knocks the focus. Then the widest and deepest view of the destination so far, too large for the window to contain. The single most spectacular second of the episode belongs here.

A gust slams the glass, the whole carriage shakes and the focus hunts. Then the deepest view yet: the camera looks down the length of the hall field, roofs stretching to the snow horizon in every direction, gate lines and banners between them, the plain too large to read. Overhead is almost black and the fires below are the only light.

HEART AND PAYOFF. Open with the train passing through or beneath something colossal. Travel alone carries it into the centre of the place. At about 8.5 seconds a calm ordinary commuter announcer quietly says the arrival line. Then the chime sounds again, the same voice begins only "Next stop-" and the shot ends mid-word while the train is still moving forward and something new is already growing ahead.

A last hard jolt and the train passes beneath a gate lintel so vast its underside fills the entire window. Out the far side, the heart of the field: firelit doorways, banners the height of the carriage, a mead lake reflecting the burning sky, roofs receding past resolution. The sky overhead is solid black, the darkest frame of the journey. The announcer says exactly: "Welcome to Valhalla."
